correctness.rationale: For all d>=2 and 0<r<1, the finite Blaschke model-space decomposition is proved by codimension-one induction and a zero-of-all-orders argument; distinct normalized Szegő kernels span the model space because their Cauchy Gram determinant is positive. Orthogonal orbit blocks reduce sharp Riesz bounds to that Gram. The Cauchy double alternant yields a pair-pseudohyperbolic determinant; direct differentiation proves -Lʺ>=((1-r²)/(2(1+r²)))². Strong Jensen and an exact cyclic variance identity give the angular deficit. For d=2 an infinitesimal displacement from antipodality proves coefficient optimality. Fourier diagonalization gives the entire regular spectrum and degree-uniform threshold. The actual packaged Python script returned 32 regular-spectral and 945 jitter comparisons plus three sharpness sequences; finite checks are supplemental only.

value.rationale: For directly measurable, unorthogonalized point-evaluation generators in a natural finite Blaschke dynamical-frame class, exact volume-optimal placement and sharp angular-jitter stability quantitatively answer which sampling geometry retains independence. All radii and degrees are covered, equality is rigid, the quadratic coefficient is truly best, and the regular-polygon spectrum yields exact frame bounds and a natural high-degree stability threshold. This is more than existence of some orthonormal orbital basis and is a motivic design/stability theorem, not an arbitrary finite computation.
